TIPC name table updates are distributed asynchronously in a cluster
entailing a risk of certain race conditions. E.g.
simultaneously issue conflicting (overlapping) publications
not be detected until both publications have reached a third node
which case one of the publications will be silently dropped on that
node. Hence
column2: we end up with an inconsistent name table.

column1: In most cases this conflict is just a temporary race
node is issuing a publication under the assumption that a previous
conflicting
column2: publication has already been withdrawn by the other node.

column1: However
column2: because of the (rtt related) distributed update delay

column1: may not yet hold true on all nodes. The symptom of this failure is a
syslog message: ""tipc: Cannot publish {%u
In this commit we add a resiliency queue at the receiving end of
the name table distributor. When insertion of an arriving publication
fails
column2: we retain it in this queue for a short amount of time

column1: that another update will arrive very soon and clear the conflict. If so
happens
The (configurable) retention value defaults to 2000 ms. Knowing from
experience that the situation described above is extremely rare
is no risk that the queue will accumulate any large number of items.
